steps: Boil a kettle and bring a large saucepan of unsalted water to the boil for the noodles.
While the water heats, slice the chicken into thin strips about 1cm wide, and cut the red pepper into short, thin strips.
Cut the carrots into thin matchsticks or grate them coarsely so they soften quickly and are safe for a toddler.
Cook the noodles for 4–5 minutes until soft, then drain and snip into short lengths with kitchen scissors.
Heat the oil in the wok over medium-high heat and fry the chicken for 5–6 minutes until white throughout with no pink. Remove it.
Stir-fry the carrot for 3 minutes and the pepper for 2 minutes until soft. Return the chicken and noodles, add the soy sauce with a splash of water, and toss for 1 minute.
pitfalls: Adding the full amount of soy sauce makes the dish too salty for a toddler, so dilute it with water and taste.
Leaving carrot in thick chunks keeps it hard and a choking risk, so cut it thin or grate it.
Overcrowding the wok steams the chicken and leaves it pale and rubbery, so cook it in two batches if needed.
output.tip: Cut the noodles and chicken into small, bite-sized pieces and let the plate cool for a few minutes before serving to your toddler.

steps: Boil a kettle and start the noodles in a large saucepan; cook for 4 minutes, then drain.
While the water heats, slice the chicken into thin strips about 1cm wide, so it cooks quickly and is easy to chew.
Cut the red pepper into thin short strips and grate the carrots, or slice them very thinly, so they soften fast for a toddler.
Heat the oil in the wok over a high heat, then stir-fry the chicken for 5–6 minutes until white throughout with no pink.
Add the carrot for 2 minutes, then the red pepper for 2 minutes, until soft enough to squash between your fingers.
Toss in the noodles with the soy sauce diluted with a splash of water, heat through for 1 minute, and cool before serving.
pitfalls: Adding the full amount of soy sauce makes the dish too salty for a toddler, so dilute it with water and taste before serving.
Thick chicken pieces cook unevenly and turn tough or stay undercooked, so slice thinly and check the centre is white.
Crunchy or long strips of carrot and pepper are a choking risk, so cut them small and cook until soft.
output.tip: Cut the noodles into short lengths with kitchen scissors after draining so they are easier for small hands to manage.

steps: Boil a kettle and bring a large saucepan of unsalted water to the boil for the noodles.
While the water heats, slice the chicken into thin strips about 1cm wide, then cut the red peppers into short, thin strips.
Peel the carrots and cut them into thin matchsticks or grate them, so they soften quickly and are easy for a toddler to chew.
Cook the noodles for 4 minutes or as the packet says, then drain and snip them into short lengths.
Heat the oil in the wok over medium-high heat and stir-fry the chicken for 5–6 minutes until white throughout with no pink.
Add the carrots and peppers and cook for 4–5 minutes until soft, then toss in the noodles with a small splash of soy sauce diluted with 2 tablespoons of water.
pitfalls: Adding the full amount of soy sauce makes the dish far too salty for a toddler, so dilute it and add only a little.
Cutting the chicken too thick leaves the centres undercooked, so slice thinly and check every piece is white inside.
Leaving noodles and vegetables in long strands or firm pieces is a choking risk, so cut everything small and cook until soft.
output.tip: Let the stir-fry cool for a few minutes and test a piece yourself before serving, as the noodles and peppers hold heat.

steps: Start the sauce first: finely chop the onion and garlic.
Heat the oil in the frying pan over medium heat, then fry the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the beef mince over high heat.
Brown the mince for 8–10 minutes, breaking up lumps, until no pink remains and it sizzles.
Stir in the tomatoes, season well, then simmer on low heat for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Boil the spaghetti in well-salted water 10 minutes before the sauce is done, drain, and toss with the sauce.
pitfalls: Crowding the pan with cold mince steams it grey and watery instead of browning, so use high heat and let it sit between stirs.
Cutting the simmer short leaves the sauce thin and acidic, so cook it until it thickens and coats a spoon.
Rinsing the cooked spaghetti washes off the starch, so the sauce slides off instead of clinging.
output.tip: Save a mugful of pasta water and loosen the sauce with a splash if it thickens too much when tossed.

steps: Fill a large saucepan with water and bring to the boil while you prep.
Finely chop the onion and garlic.
Heat the oil in the frying pan over medium-high heat, then brown the beef mince in two batches for 5–6 minutes each.
Stir in the onion for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes with a splash of water, season well, then simmer on low heat for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cook the spaghetti in well-salted water for 10–11 minutes until al dente, reserve a mug of pasta water, drain, then toss with the sauce.
pitfalls: Crowding the pan makes the beef mince steam and turn grey instead of browning, so cook it in batches.
Burnt garlic turns bitter and spoils the sauce, so add it for only 1 minute before the tomatoes.
Rinsing the cooked spaghetti washes off the starch, so the sauce slides off instead of clinging.
output.tip: Toss the drained spaghetti in the sauce with a splash of pasta water over low heat for 1 minute so it coats every strand.

steps: Fill a large saucepan with salted water and bring it to the boil on a high heat.
Finely chop the onion and garlic while the water heats.
Heat the olive oil in the frying pan over medium heat and soften the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the beef mince, breaking it up and browning it over high heat for 8–10 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes, season well, then simmer on low heat for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cook the spaghetti for 9–10 minutes in the last stretch of simmering, then reserve a mugful of pasta water and drain.
pitfalls: Crowding the pan with mince steams it grey instead of browning it, so use a wide pan and let it sizzle undisturbed.
Burnt garlic turns the sauce bitter, so add it only after the onion has softened and cook it for no more than 30 seconds.
Draining the spaghetti and leaving it to sit makes it stick together, so combine it with the sauce straight away.
output.tip: Toss the drained spaghetti in the sauce with a splash of the starchy pasta water so it clings to every strand.

steps: Dice the onion and red pepper into 1cm pieces, then heat the oil in the pan over medium heat.
Fry the onion and pepper for 8–10 minutes, until soft and lightly golden.
While they soften, slice the bread and crack the eggs into a small bowl.
Stir in the cumin for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes and season with salt and pepper.
Simmer for 8–10 minutes, until thick and jammy, then make four wells and slide in the eggs.
Cover and cook on low heat for 5–7 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks still wobble. Serve with the bread.
pitfalls: Adding eggs to thin, watery sauce makes them sink and break up, so reduce the sauce until it coats a spoon.
Cooking the eggs on high heat leaves rubbery whites and hard yolks, so keep the heat low and the lid on.
Skipping the seasoning before the eggs go in leaves the sauce bland, because the eggs can't be seasoned through.
output.tip: Warm the bread in a low oven for the last few minutes so it stays crusty and ready for mopping.

steps: Dice the onion and red pepper into 1cm pieces.
Heat the oil in the pan over medium heat, then fry the onion and pepper for 7–8 minutes until soft.
Stir in the cumin for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Simmer the sauce for 8–10 minutes, until thick enough to leave a trail when you drag a spoon through it.
Make four wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook on low heat for 5–6 minutes until the whites are set.
While the eggs cook, slice or warm the bread; serve straight from the pan.
pitfalls: Adding the eggs to thin, watery sauce makes them spread and the whites stay runny, so reduce the sauce first.
Cooking the eggs on high heat leaves the yolks hard and the bases catching, so keep the heat low and covered.
Under-cooking the pepper and onion leaves the sauce raw and sharp, so soften them for at least 7 minutes.
output.tip: Crack each egg into a small bowl first so you can slide it into the sauce without breaking the yolk.

steps: Dice the onion and red pepper into 1cm pieces.
Fry them in olive oil over medium heat for 8–10 minutes, until soft and lightly golden.
Stir in the cumin for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes with a good pinch of salt and pepper.
Simmer the sauce for 8–10 minutes, until thick and jammy.
Make four wells in the sauce and crack in the eggs. Cover and cook on low heat for 5–6 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks wobble.
While the eggs cook, slice the bread and warm or toast it. Serve straight from the pan.
pitfalls: Adding eggs to thin, watery sauce makes them sink and the whites spread, so reduce the sauce until it coats a spoon.
Cooking the eggs on high heat with the lid on turns the yolks hard and chalky, so keep the heat low and check at 5 minutes.
Under-seasoning the sauce leaves the dish flat, as the eggs and bread dilute the flavour, so taste before adding the eggs.
output.tip: Crack each egg into a small bowl first so you can slide it gently into the sauce and avoid broken yolks or stray shell.

steps: Take the beef out of the fridge 1 hour ahead, rub with oil, garlic, rosemary, thyme and pepper, and heat the oven to 220°C.
Sear and roast the beef at 220°C for 20 minutes, then drop to 180°C and roast 1 hour for medium, to 55°C inside.
While the beef roasts, peel and cut the potatoes and parsnips, parboil the potatoes for 8 minutes, then drain and shake roughly.
Heat oil in the heavy tray until smoking, add the potatoes, parsnips and carrots, and roast for 1 hour 15 minutes, turning once.
Whisk the flour, eggs and milk with salt into a batter and rest it. When the beef comes out, rest it under foil for 30 minutes.

Raise the oven to 220°C and heat oil in the tin until smoking, then pour in the batter and bake 20–25 minutes. Meanwhile, simmer the stock and wine with the tin juices for the gravy, steam the broccoli for 4 minutes and serve with the horseradish.
pitfalls: Opening the oven door during the first 15 minutes of baking makes the Yorkshire puddings collapse, so keep it shut.
Carving the beef straight from the oven lets the juices run out and leaves the meat dry, so rest it for 30 minutes.
Putting the batter into lukewarm fat gives flat, greasy puddings, so heat the oil until it smokes first.
output.tip: Dry the parboiled potatoes in the colander for 5 minutes and rough up their edges so they roast extra crisp.

steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Take the beef out of the fridge, rub with oil, salt, pepper, crushed garlic, rosemary and thyme.
Peel and chop the potatoes, parboil for 8–10 minutes, then drain and shake to roughen the edges. Peel and chop the carrots and parsnips.
Roast the beef at 220°C for 20 minutes, then lower to 180°C for about 1 hour for medium. Rest it for 30 minutes under foil.

While the beef roasts, whisk the batter and rest it. Heat oil in the large tray for 10 minutes, add the potatoes and roast for 60 minutes, turning once. Add the carrots and parsnips with the butter after 20 minutes.
Raise the oven to 220°C when the beef comes out. Pour batter into the smoking-hot oiled Yorkshire tin and bake for 20–25 minutes without opening the door.
While the puddings bake, simmer the wine and stock with the beef juices for 10 minutes to make gravy. Steam the broccoli for 4–5 minutes, then carve the beef and serve with horseradish.
pitfalls: Opening the oven during the first 15 minutes makes the Yorkshire puddings collapse, so keep the door shut.
Pouring batter into lukewarm fat gives flat, greasy puddings, so heat the oil until it smokes lightly.
Carving the beef straight from the oven lets the juices run out and leaves the meat dry, so rest it for 30 minutes.
output.tip: Use the beef's resting time to your advantage: the oven is free for the Yorkshire puddings, and the foil-covered meat stays warm.

steps: Heat the oven to 220°C, then take the beef out of the fridge. Rub it with oil, salt, pepper, rosemary and thyme.
Whisk the flour, eggs, milk and a pinch of salt into a smooth batter. Rest it for at least 30 minutes.
Parboil the peeled potatoes for 8–10 minutes, drain and shake roughly. Roast them in hot oil on a tray at the top of the oven for 60–70 minutes, turning once.
Sear the beef in the roasting tin for 15 minutes at 220°C, then lower to 180°C. Roast for about 1 hour for medium, to 55–60°C in the centre.
While the beef roasts, toss the carrots and parsnips with butter and garlic. Add them to the oven for the last 40 minutes.

Rest the beef under foil for 30 minutes. Heat the Yorkshire tin with oil at 220°C for 10 minutes, pour in the batter and bake 20–25 minutes. Meanwhile make gravy from the beef tin juices, wine and stock, and steam the broccoli for 4–5 minutes.
pitfalls: Opening the oven door while the Yorkshire puddings rise makes them collapse, so keep it shut for the first 20 minutes.
Pouring batter into lukewarm fat gives flat, greasy puddings, so wait until the oil is smoking hot.
Carving the beef straight from the oven lets the juices run out and leaves the meat dry, so rest it for 30 minutes.
output.tip: Use the beef resting time to free up the oven for the Yorkshire puddings, which need the highest heat of the whole meal.

pitfalls: Adding the chicken straight from the marinade into a crowded pan steams it rather than browning it, so brown it in two batches and scrape off excess yoghurt first.
Pouring cold tomatoes onto a boiling base and then boiling hard can make the yoghurt residue split and turn the sauce grainy, so keep it at a gentle simmer.
Leaving the rice unrinsed and unrested gives sticky, clumped grains, so rinse 300g until the water runs clear and rest it, covered, for 5 minutes after cooking.
output.tip: Finish with a small spoonful of yoghurt or a splash of double cream and a pinch of salt off the heat to round out the acidity of the tomatoes.

pitfalls: Adding the tomatoes straight from the can without cooking them down means the sauce tastes sharp and thin, so let it bubble uncovered for the last 5–10 minutes until it thickens.
Frying the onion over too high a heat leaves bitter, scorched edges rather than sweetness, so keep it at medium and add a splash of water if it catches.
Cooking the rice at the same time as the curry without a plan leaves it sticky or cold, so rinse it until the water runs clear and start it about 15 minutes before the curry finishes.
output.tip: Stir a spoonful of yoghurt or a splash of double cream into the curry off the heat at the end to mellow the spice and give a glossy finish, and scatter over chopped coriander.

pitfalls: Adding the chicken straight from the marinade to a pan that is not hot enough steams it grey instead of browning it, so wipe off excess yoghurt and let the pan heat up first.
Pouring in the tomatoes while the pan is still very hot, or boiling the sauce hard, can make the yoghurt on the chicken split and turn grainy; keep it at a gentle simmer.
Cooking the rice with no seasoning or rinsing leaves it sticky and bland, so rinse 300g until the water runs clear and cook it in about 600ml of salted water while the curry simmers.
output.tip: Finish with a small squeeze of lemon juice and a handful of chopped coriander off the heat to lift the flavour of the sauce.

pitfalls: Cooking the rice noodles in the wok without soaking or boiling them first leaves them hard in the middle or gummy, so soak them in hot water until just tender, then drain well.
Adding soy sauce to a crowded, cool wok makes the vegetables stew and the tofu coating turn soggy, so keep the heat high and sauce the dish only at the end.
Crowding the frying pan with tofu cubes drops the oil temperature and the cornstarch coating sticks and tears, so fry in 2 batches with 1cm of oil heated to about 180°C.
output.tip: Cut the broccoli into small, even florets and add 2 tablespoons of water to the wok for the last minute, covered, so it turns tender-crisp and bright green.

pitfalls: Cooking the rice noodles straight in the wok without soaking or boiling them first leaves them hard in places and gummy in others, so soak or boil them to just tender and drain well beforehand.
Adding the soy sauce while the tofu is still in the pan, or leaving the crisp tofu to sit in the sauce, turns the coating soggy, so keep the tofu separate until the final 30 seconds of tossing.
Overcrowding the frying pan with all the tofu at once drops the temperature and makes the cornstarch coating patchy and stuck, so fry in two batches with a thin layer of hot oil.
output.tip: Cut the broccoli into small florets of about 3cm and add a splash of water to the wok for the last minute, covered, so the stalks turn tender-crisp without extra pans.

pitfalls: Cooking the rice noodles in the wok without soaking or boiling them first leaves them hard in places and gummy in others, so soak or boil them until just tender and drain well before they go in.
Adding the soy sauce straight onto the crisp tofu, or leaving the tofu in the pan too long at the end, softens the coating, so toss it through for under 30 seconds.
Putting large broccoli florets in raw means the outsides burn before the stalks soften, so cut them into pieces of about 2–3cm and add a splash of water to steam briefly.
output.tip: Dry the pressed tofu with kitchen paper and shake off excess cornstarch before frying in a thin layer of hot oil, as this gives a thin, even crust that stays crisp.

steps: Pane riisi keema esimesena: loputa riis, lisa potti vesi ja keeda kaane all 12–15 minutit, ära lisa vette soola.
Haki sibul peenelt ja riivi porgand jämedalt, lõika kanafilee 2 cm kuubikuteks.
Kuumuta pann keskmisel kuumusel, hauta sibul ja porgand 5 minutit pehmeks.
Lisa kana ja prae 5–6 minutit, kuni see on igalt poolt valkjas.
Murra puljongikuubik 200 ml kuuma vette, lisa pannile ja hauta kaane all 8–10 minutit. Maitse enne soolamist, kuubik annab juba piisavalt soola.
Sega hapukoor kuumutatud kastmesse, soojenda 1–2 minutit ilma keetmata ja serveeri riisiga.
pitfalls: Ära lisa kanale ega riisile lisasoola enne maitsmist: puljongikuubik on soolane ja väikesele lapsele läheb roog liiga soolaseks.
Ära keeda kastet pärast hapukoore lisamist: hapukoor lõheneb ja kaste muutub tükiliseks.
Ära prae kanatükke liiga kaua: filee muutub kuivaks ja kõvaks.
output.tip: Kui laps sööb kaasa, kasuta pool puljongikuubikut ja lisa maitseks natuke pipart või tilli, siis jääb roog hoopis vähem soolane.

equipment: Keskmise suurusega kaanega pott riisi jaoks
steps: Pane riis potti, vala peale külma vett ja keeda kaane all 12–15 minutit pehmeks. Soola vette vaid näpuotsatäis või jäta üldse soolamata.
Haki sibul peeneks ja riivi porgandid jämedalt, kuni vesi keeb.
Lõika kanafilee 2 cm tükkideks ja prae kuumal pannil õlis 5–6 minutit kuldseks.
Lisa sibul ja porgand ning hauta 5 minutit pehmeks.
Lahusta puljongikuubik 200 ml kuumas vees, vala pannile ja hauta kaane all 8 minutit. Sega sisse hapukoor ja soojenda 2 minutit, ära lase keema.
Maitse kaste enne lõppu ja lisa soola vaid vajadusel, puljongikuubik annab juba soolast maitset. Serveeri riisiga.
pitfalls: Ära pane puljongikuubikut ja lisaks veel soola kohe algul: kaste muutub liiga soolaseks ja väikesele lapsele ei sobi.
Ära keeda kastet pärast hapukoore lisamist: hapukoor hakkab kalgenema.
Ära prae kanatükke liiga kaua: liha kuivab ja muutub kõvaks.
output.tip: Soola kaste alles lõpus, vajadusel lisa laua peal täiskasvanutele, et väike laps saaks sama toitu vähese soolaga.

equipment: Suur sügav pann või kastrul kaanega
steps: Pane riis koos veega kaanega potti keema ja lisa puljongikuubik vaid poole kuubiku ulatuses, et soola jääks vähem.
Haki sibul peenelt ja riivi porgand jämedalt, samal ajal kui riisivesi kuumeneb.
Lõika kanafilee 2 cm kuubikuteks ja kuumuta pannil õli.
Prae kana keskmisel kuumusel 5–6 minutit, kuni pind on valge ja kergelt pruunistunud.
Lisa sibul ja porgand ning hauta kaane all 8–10 minutit, kuni köögivili on pehme.
Sega hapukoor juurde, kuumuta 2–3 minutit ilma keetmata, maitse ja lisa soola ainult vajadusel. Serveeri valmis riisiga.
pitfalls: Ära lisa puljongikuupi tervelt ja soola peale: kuup on juba soolane ning roog läheb väikesele lapsele liiga soolaseks.
Ära keeda hapukoort kõrgel kuumusel: see hakkab kokku kerkima ja kaste muutub tükiliseks.
Ära prae kanatükke liiga kaua: filee kuivab ja muutub kummiseks.
output.tip: Maitsesta roog alles lõpus ja lisa laua peal täiskasvanutele soola eraldi, siis saab väike laps sama toitu ilma lisasoolata.

steps: Leota odrakruupe külmas vees ja pane hapukapsas kurnis nõrguma; vajadusel loputa kapsast, kui see on väga hapu.
Lõika sealiha 3 cm kuubikuteks ja haki sibul peeneks.
Prae liha poti põhjas kuumas rasvas igast küljest pruuniks, siis lisa sibul ja prae 2–3 minutit pehmeks.
Lisa hapukapsas, loorberilehed ja kurnatud odrakruubid, kalla peale vett nii, et see katab poole sisust, ja hauta kaane all vaiksel tulel 1 tund.
Kuni pott podiseb, kooritud kartulid lõika 3 cm tükkideks ja lisa potti, kui kapsas on veerand tunni pärast pooleldi pehme.
Hauta veel 45–60 minutit, kuni liha, kruubid ja kartul on pehmed, sega aeg-ajalt ja lisa vajadusel vett; maitsesta lõpus soolaga.
pitfalls: Ära soola enne hauduma panekut: hapukapsas ja liha annavad soolsust juurde ning roog võib minna liiga soolaseks.
Ära jäta potti järelevalveta ilma vedelikuta: kruubid ja kapsas kleepuvad põhja ja kõrbevad.
Ära lõika kartuleid liiga väikeseks ega lisa liiga vara: need keevad pudruks ja roog kaotab konsistentsi.
output.tip: Mulgikapsad maitsevad järgmisel päeval veel paremini, sest maitsed jõuavad üksteisega kokku sulada.

steps: Leota odrakruupe külmas vees, kui neil on selleks aega, ja loputa need enne keetmist läbi.
Lõika sealiha 3 cm kuubikuteks ja haki sibul peeneks.
Prae liha potis kuumal rasval kuldpruuniks, vajadusel kahes jaos, ja lisa sibul viimase 2 minuti jooksul.
Lisa hapukapsas, odrakruup, loorberilehed ja nii palju vett, et see katab need peaaegu täielikult. Lase keema tõusta, kata kaanega ja hauta madalal tulel 1 tund.
Kooru ja tükelda kartulid, lisa potti ning hauta veel 40–50 minutit, kuni kruubid ja kartul on pehmed.
Sega aeg-ajalt ja lisa vajadusel kuuma vett. Lõpuks muserda osa kartuleid lusika või tuhkriga, et roog muutuks paksuks, ja maitsesta soolaga.
pitfalls: Ära jäta potti järelvalveta ilma vedelikku kontrollimata: põhi kõrbeb kergesti ära ja roog hakkab kibedalt maitsema.
Ära lisa kartuleid liiga vara: need keevad pudruks ja roog kaotab oma struktuuri.
Ära jäta hapukapsast loputamata, kui see on väga hapu: roog võib tulla liiga terav ja soolane.
output.tip: Lase valmis mulgikapsastel enne serveerimist 10–15 minutit kaane all seista, siis tõmbuvad maitsed kokku ja konsistents muutub paremaks.

steps: Leota odrakruupe külmas vees, kuni alustad ülejäänud toiduvalmistamist, ja loputa need enne keetmist.
Lõika sealiha 3 cm kuubikuteks ja haki sibul peeneks.
Prae liha potis kuumas rasvas kuldpruuniks ja lisa sibul, prae 2–3 minutit pehmeks.
Lisa hapukapsas, loorberilehed ja nii palju vett, et see katab liha poolenisti, kata kaanega ja hauta madalal kuumusel 40 minutit.
Lisa loputatud odrakruubid ja hauta veel 30 minutit, sega aeg-ajalt ja lisa vajadusel vett.
Prae või keeda kartulid eraldi pehmeks, 20–25 minutit, ja serveeri need kapsaste kõrvale.
pitfalls: Ära jäta odrakruupe loputamata: tärklis teeb roa liiga limaseks ja kleepuvaks.
Ära hauta liiga kõrgel kuumusel ega ilma vedelikuta: kapsas kõrbeb põhja ja muutub kibedaks.
Ära jäta liha pruunistamata: roog jääb lamedama maitsega.
output.tip: Lase valmis mulgikapsastel enne serveerimist 10 minutit kaane all seista, siis tõmbavad maitsed paremini kokku.

pitfalls: Ära jäta kartuliviile paksuks (üle 5 mm): 20 minutiga ei küpse need läbi ja lõhe on valmis enne kartuleid.
Ära pane kartuleid ahju ilma õli ja soolata: viilud kuivavad, kleepuvad plaadile kinni ega saa maitset.
Ära lisa lõhet külmkapi külmana otse kuumadele kartulitele: väljast kuivab ja seest jääb toorem.
output.tip: Pane lõhe nahaga pool allapoole ja tilguta peale veidi oliiviõli, siis jääb kala mahlane ja nahk ei kleepu külge.

pitfalls: Ära lõika kartuliviile liiga paksuks (üle 5 mm): need jäävad 20 minuti pärast keskelt toored, kui lõhe peale läheb.
Ära jäta kartuleid ilma õlita ahjuplaadile: viilud kleepuvad külge ja kuivavad servadest, mitte ei pruunistu.
Ära pane lõhet külmkapi külmana otse kuumadele kartulitele: filee küpseb ebaühtlaselt ja keskosa jääb toorem kui servad.
output.tip: Kuivata lõhefilee enne maitsestamist paberrätikuga ja võta see 15 minutit varem külmkapist välja, siis küpseb liha ühtlaselt ja jääb mahlane.

pitfalls: Ära jäta kartuliviile paksemaks kui 5 mm: 20 minutiga ei küpse need läbi ja lõhe on valmis enne kartuleid.
Ära pane kartuleid ilma õli ja soolata ahju: need kuivavad, jäävad kahvatuks ja kleepuvad plaadi külge.
Ära lisa sidrunimahla kartulitele enne lõhe peale panemist ega jäta kala sidrunimahlaga seisma: hape muudab kala pinna kuivaks ja kõvaks.
output.tip: Kuivata lõhefilee paberrätikuga ja pane see nahk allpool kartulite peale, siis jääb kala mahlane ja nahk ei kleepu kinni.

pitfalls: Ära vala sulavõid taignasse liiga kuumana: muna hakkab kokku kerkima ja taigen jääb tombuliseks.
Ära pane taignat pannile enne, kui pann on korralikult kuum: pannkook jääb kahvatuks, imab rasva ja rebeneb keerates.
Ära tee pannkooke liiga paksuks ega vala pannile liiga palju taignat korraga: need küpsevad keskelt toorelt ja ei veni õhukeseks.
output.tip: Määri pann esimese pannkoogi jaoks kergelt võiga ja kalla taigen kulbiga (umbes 60–70 ml) pannile, keera pann kohe ringi, et taigen laiali valguks.

pitfalls: Ära vala sulavõid taignasse kuumana: see võib muna kohupiimataoliseks muuta ja taigen jääb tombuline.
Ära vala taignat pannile liiga palju korraga: pannkook jääb paks ja kummine ning ei keeras ilusti ümber.
Ära hoia panni liiga kuumana: pannkook pruunistub väljastpoolt kiiresti, aga sisu jääb toores ja serv kõrbeb.
output.tip: Määri esimese pannkoogi jaoks pann õhukeselt võiga ja tee see proovikook: kui see on liiga paks, vesinda taigent 2–3 spl piimaga.

pitfalls: Ära vala sulatatud võid taignasse kuumana: see võib munad osaliselt kinni keeta ja tainas jääb tükiline.
Ära lisa jahu korraga kogu piimaga: jahutükid jäävad taigna sisse ja neid on hiljem raske lahti vispeldada.
Ära keera pann liiga kuumaks ega jäta seda liiga leigeks: liiga kuumal pannil põleb pind enne, kui tainas hangub, leigel aga jäävad pannkoogid kahvatuks ja kummised.
output.tip: Määri pann esimese pannkoogi jaoks õhukeselt võiga ja vala tainast umbes 60 ml korraga, siis saad ühtlaselt õhukesed pannkoogid.
